Calculate and interpret average rate of change and estimate instantaneous rate of change

sections.title: Multiple choice
sections.instructions: Circle one answer per question; each question is worth one mark.

ordering_rules: Use 20 consecutive multiple-choice questions, each worth exactly one mark.
Start with functions, domain/range, transformations, and inverses; finish with diagram and rate reasoning.
Include original endpoint, circular-ride, and secant-tangent diagrams.

progression_notes: Diagram and rate interpretation near the end

diagram_expectations: Original labelled endpoint graph for domain reasoning
Original circular-ride diagram shared by two one-mark questions
Original secant-tangent diagram shared by two one-mark questions

trap_patterns.description: Confusing open and closed interval or piecewise endpoints
Using k instead of 1/k in a point mapping
Confusing inverse with reciprocal or omitting a domain restriction
Confusing secant slope with tangent slope or omitting units

generation_rules.variation_policy: Create 20 fresh one-mark multiple-choice questions across the established Unit 1 topics, with four options each and one correct choice.
freshness_requirements: No verbatim textbook or public sample stems
constraints: Use only one-mark questions, with 20 questions and 20 marks total.
Stay within the supplied Unit 1 index.
Include a few original diagram-based thinking questions.
Provide a compact student PDF and separate answer key.
